stamped-lock-concept.title: Coordinate advanced read/write access with StampedLock
stamped-lock-concept.short: Use write, read, or optimistic-read stamps explicitly
stamped-lock-concept.summary: StampedLock provides exclusive writes, shared reads, and optimistic reads represented by stamps.
stamped-lock-concept.why: Optimistic reads can reduce read-side coordination when data can be validated before the result is used.
stamped-lock-concept.tips: StampedLock is not reentrant; always pair successful lock acquisition with the matching unlock operation and validate optimistic reads.

primitive-streams-concept.title: Use primitive streams for numeric pipelines
primitive-streams-concept.short: Process int, long, and double values without boxing each element
primitive-streams-concept.summary: IntStream, LongStream, and DoubleStream provide stream operations specialized for primitive numeric values.
primitive-streams-concept.why: They avoid repeated boxing and expose numeric operations such as sum, average, and range.
primitive-streams-concept.tips: Convert with boxed only when an object Stream or collection is actually needed.

map-entry-copy-of.title: Snapshot a map entry with Map.Entry.copyOf
map-entry-copy-of.short: Detach a key-value pair from a mutable map entry
map-entry-copy-of.summary: Map.Entry.copyOf creates an unmodifiable entry containing the same key and value as another entry.
map-entry-copy-of.why: Entries obtained from mutable maps may remain tied to map state, while a copied entry is suitable for retaining independently.
map-entry-copy-of.tips: The copied entry rejects null keys or values and does not deep-copy the key or value objects.

stream-iterate-predicate.title: Generate bounded streams with Stream.iterate
stream-iterate-predicate.short: Stop an iterative stream with a predicate
stream-iterate-predicate.summary: The three-argument Stream.iterate generates successive values while a hasNext predicate remains true.
stream-iterate-predicate.why: It expresses finite iterative sequences without combining an infinite stream with a separate limiting operation.
stream-iterate-predicate.tips: Make sure the next function progresses toward making the predicate false.

file-system-not-found-exception.title: FileSystemNotFoundException
file-system-not-found-exception.short: Look up only file systems that have already been created
file-system-not-found-exception.summary: FileSystemNotFoundException indicates that no file system is available for a URI through the requested provider lookup.
file-system-not-found-exception.why: FileSystems.getFileSystem retrieves an existing file system; it does not create one when none has been established.
file-system-not-found-exception.tips: Use the appropriate provider or newFileSystem when creation is required, and manage the created file system's lifetime explicitly.

closed-file-system-exception.title: ClosedFileSystemException
closed-file-system-exception.short: Do not use a file system after it has been closed
closed-file-system-exception.summary: ClosedFileSystemException indicates an operation was attempted on a FileSystem that is no longer open.
closed-file-system-exception.why: Paths and providers associated with explicitly managed file systems may depend on that file system's lifetime.
closed-file-system-exception.tips: Keep resource lifetime clear and close custom file systems only after all dependent work has finished.

var-compound-declaration-error.title: var cannot declare multiple variables at once
var-compound-declaration-error.short: Split inferred local variables into separate declarations
var-compound-declaration-error.summary: A local variable declaration using var must declare exactly one variable.
var-compound-declaration-error.why: Local variable type inference is defined from the initializer of one declarator, so compound declarations are not permitted.
var-compound-declaration-error.tips: Write one var declaration per local variable or use an explicit type where a compound declaration is clearer.

lambda-var-mixed-parameters-error.title: Do not mix var and implicit lambda parameters
lambda-var-mixed-parameters-error.short: Use var on every lambda parameter or none of them
lambda-var-mixed-parameters-error.summary: When var is used in a lambda parameter list, every parameter in that list must use var.
lambda-var-mixed-parameters-error.why: Java requires a consistent parameter declaration form within one lambda expression.
lambda-var-mixed-parameters-error.tips: Use var consistently when parameter annotations need it; otherwise omit var from all parameters.

this-escape-warning.title: this-escape warning
this-escape-warning.short: Do not expose an incompletely constructed object from a constructor
this-escape-warning.summary: The javac this-escape lint warning detects constructor behavior that can expose this before construction of a subclass is complete.
this-escape-warning.why: Calling overridable methods or otherwise leaking this during construction can let code observe fields before subclass initialization has finished.
this-escape-warning.tips: Keep constructors from invoking overridable behavior or publishing this; perform such work after construction when possible.

string-split-regex-dot-trap.title: String.split treats its argument as a regular expression
string-split-regex-dot-trap.short: Escape a literal dot before splitting on it
string-split-regex-dot-trap.summary: String.split receives a regular expression, so a plain dot matches any character rather than only a period.
string-split-regex-dot-trap.why: Code that visually resembles splitting on punctuation can therefore produce surprising empty or fragmented results.
string-split-regex-dot-trap.tips: Escape regex metacharacters or use Pattern.quote when the delimiter comes from literal text.
